T-SQL's DAY(x), MONTH(x) and YEAR(x) accept a date or a string, but transpiling them to Postgres gives functions Postgres does not have. # expected:  SELECT EXTRACT(DAY FROM CAST(x AS DATE)), EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(x AS DATE)), EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(x AS DATE))

T-SQL's DAY(x), MONTH(x) and YEAR(x) accept a date or a string, but transpiling them to Postgres gives functions Postgres does not have. They should become EXTRACT(DAY FROM CAST(x AS DATE)) and so on in Postgres (no cast needed when the argument is already known to be a DATE after type annotation, and an unsupported error when its type is known not to be a date), and T-SQL round-trips must not gain casts.

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

transpile("SELECT DAY(x), MONTH(x), YEAR(x)", read="tsql", write="postgres")[0]
# currently: SELECT DAY(x), MONTH(x), YEAR(x)
# expected:  SELECT EXTRACT(DAY FROM CAST(x AS DATE)), EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(x AS DATE)), EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(x AS DATE))
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
